newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrins hurl eggs, stones at Serb socialists.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrins hurl eggs, stones at Serb socialists.

text.p: Several thousand demonstrators in Podgorica, the capital of Montenegro, threw stones, eggs and tomatoes at a motorcade of senior ruling Serbian Socialist Party (SPS) officials on Monday.
The SPS delegation was arriving for talks with embattled Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic, independent Serbian B92 radio reported.

Some of the demonstrators carried banners reading "Momo (Bulatovic), you can dye your hair blond, too" -- an allusion to the son of Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic -- and "Bulatovic, you sold off Prevlaka, but you will not sell Montenegro".
The Prevlaka peninsula, south of Dubrovnik, borders Montenegro, but most of it is controlled by Croatia.
Bulatovic was ousted as president of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists earlier this month by a reformist faction led by Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
Montenegro, the junior partner to Serbia in what remains of Yugoslavia after its violent 1991 break-up, is home to some 650,000 people and generates five percent of Yugoslavia's GDP.

It has refused to wait for Serbia to press on with its own radical economic reforms. Djukanovic has urged Milosevic to pursue reform, democratise the country and reintegrate it into the international community.
Milosevic backs Bulatovic in the power struggle and the SPS visit to Podgorica is seen in the Belgrade press as an attempt to boost his beleaguered election campaign.
Montenegrin parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic has called presidential elections for October 5, practically three months before Bulatovic's current mandate expires.
